learning_outcomes.text: Define a thermodynamic system for practical problems.
Set up mass, energy, and entropy balances for closed and open systems.
Make reasonable, realistic assumptions for subsequent analysis.
Determine material properties (pressure, temperature, density, internal thermal energy, enthalpy, entropy, exergy) using various methods.
Select and apply suitable thermal and caloric equations of state, steam tables, state diagrams (especially: p,T-, p,v-, T,s-, h,s-, log(p),h-, h_{1+X},X-diagrams) for determining material properties.
Perform calculations and representations of steady and unsteady, reversible and irreversible processes of gases and liquids/vapors.

Understand, calculate, discuss, and evaluate the most important technical cyclic processes regarding their efficiency (Cyclic processes: at least Carnot, Joule, Stirling, Philips, Otto, Diesel, Clausius-Rankine, Plank processes).
Present and interpret considerations and results using common (graphical) representation forms (plant diagrams, state diagrams, Sankey diagrams) of thermodynamics.
Understand the quantities relative humidity and water content and thus evaluate the consequences of state changes such as heating, cooling, dehumidifying, or mixing.
Recognize heat transfer phenomena and calculate them for simple cases.
During tutorials, students work in small groups, learning about group dynamic processes when solving technical problems.
Students are able to select appropriate methods to systematically analyze thermal machines and systems and evaluate the results.

syllabus_topics: Thermodynamic state variables and changes of state
First and Second Law of Thermodynamics
Energy, mass, and entropy balances of technical systems
Ideal and real gases as well as thermal material models
Cyclic processes and thermodynamic processes in technical applications
Heat transfer and energy conversion in thermal systems
Analysis and evaluation of thermodynamic processes and efficiencies
Application of thermodynamic methods to energy technology problems
assessment_rules: Students must achieve at least 75% of the maximum possible points in homework assignments to be admitted to the exam. The final grade is based on a 120-minute written exam.
